parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of sound energy?
explanation_steps: Sound is produced by vibrations. A drum skin or a guitar string moves quickly back and forth, and this makes sound.
A lamp gives light, a dynamo gives electricity, and wood is a fuel (chemical energy).
So the source of sound energy here is vibration. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 66; Science Grade 6, p. 52)
questions.explain_simple: Sound comes from things that vibrate (move quickly back and forth).
tips: No vibration → no sound.

similar_questions.stem: When you pluck a guitar string, the sound comes from
explanation_steps: The string vibrates, and the vibration makes sound.

questions.stem: The mechanical advantage of a machine is 4. If the load is 100 N, calculate the effort.
explanation_steps: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort, so effort = load ÷ M.A.
Effort = 100 N ÷ 4 = 25 N.
Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 5)
questions.explain_simple: Effort = load ÷ M.A. = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 N.
tips: M.A = L ÷ E. So E = L ÷ M.A and L = M.A × E.

similar_questions.stem: A lever lifts a load of 600 N with an effort of 200 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
explanation_steps: M.A = load ÷ effort = 600 ÷ 200 = 3.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a magnetic substance?
explanation_steps: Magnetic substances are attracted by a magnet. Iron (and steel, nickel, cobalt) are magnetic.
Cloth, wood and plastic are not attracted by a magnet: they are non-magnetic. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 173)
questions.explain_simple: A magnet pulls iron. So iron is a magnetic substance.
tips: Magnetic: iron, steel, nickel, cobalt. Most other things are non-magnetic.

similar_questions.stem: Which object will a magnet pick up?

options.A: a paper clip made of steel

explanation_steps: Steel contains iron, so the magnet attracts the steel paper clip.

questions.stem: Sound can travel through the following, except:
explanation_steps: Sound is carried by vibrating particles, so it needs matter (a medium).
Solids, liquids and gases have particles, so sound travels through them.
A vacuum is empty space with no particles. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 207)
questions.explain_simple: Sound needs particles to move. A vacuum has none, so sound cannot go through it.
tips: In space there is no air, so there is no sound.

similar_questions.stem: Astronauts on the Moon talk to each other by radio because

options.B: sound cannot travel where there is no air

explanation_steps: The Moon has no air (almost a vacuum), so sound cannot travel there.

questions.stem: In the human circulatory system the largest artery is:
explanation_steps: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
The largest artery is the aorta. It carries blood from the left ventricle to the body.
The vena cava is a vein, and capillaries and arterioles are very small vessels. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 19)
questions.explain_simple: The aorta is the biggest artery in the body.
tips: Aorta = largest artery. Vena cava = largest vein.

similar_questions.stem: Which blood vessel brings blood from the body back to the heart?
explanation_steps: The venae cavae are veins that bring blood back to the right auricle.

questions.stem: The type of joint that allows movement in all directions is:
explanation_steps: A ball and socket joint (hip and shoulder) lets the bone move in all directions.
A hinge joint (elbow, knee) moves in one plane only, like a door. Fixed (immovable) joints do not move, like in the skull.
Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 30)
questions.explain_simple: The shoulder and hip joints move in all directions. They are ball and socket joints.
tips: Ball and socket = all directions; hinge = one direction.

similar_questions.stem: The knee joint moves only forward and back. It is a
explanation_steps: The knee moves in one plane only, like a door hinge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the kind of friction between two surfaces that are moving over each other?
explanation_steps: There are two kinds of friction: static and dynamic.
Static friction acts between surfaces that are not moving. Dynamic friction acts between two surfaces that are moving over each other (sliding or rolling).
All friction opposes (works against) motion, so C and D are false. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 30)
questions.explain_simple: When surfaces move over each other, the friction is dynamic friction.
tips: Static = not moving; dynamic = moving (sliding or rolling).

similar_questions.stem: A heavy box is on the floor. You push it but it does not move. Which friction stops it?
explanation_steps: The box is not moving, so the friction is static friction.

questions.stem: The cells important for sexual reproduction are:
explanation_steps: Sexual reproduction needs sex cells (gametes).
The male sex cell is the sperm cell and the female sex cell is the egg cell. They join at fertilization.
Nerve, muscle, skin and blood cells are body cells. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 204)
questions.explain_simple: A sperm cell and an egg cell join to make a new baby.
tips: Sex cells = sperm (male) + egg (female). All others are body cells.

similar_questions.stem: Which cells are made by the testes?
explanation_steps: The testes produce sperm cells at puberty.

questions.stem: One of the following is an organ of the human digestive system. Identify it:
explanation_steps: The digestive system includes the mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum and anus (and the liver and pancreas).
The kidney is in the excretory system, the skull in the skeletal system, and the heart in the circulatory system. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 3)
questions.explain_simple: The stomach digests food. It is part of the digestive system.
tips: Digestive system = the food tube from mouth to anus.

similar_questions.stem: Which organ is part of the digestive system?
explanation_steps: Food is digested and absorbed in the small intestine.

questions.stem: When an object is cooled it decreases in size. This is known as:
explanation_steps: Materials get bigger when heated (expansion) and smaller when cooled (contraction).
Reflection is about light or heat bouncing back, and conduction is a way heat moves. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 118-119)
questions.explain_simple: Getting smaller when cold is called contraction.
tips: Hot → expand. Cold → contract.

similar_questions.stem: A metal ball fits through a ring. After heating, it does not fit. This is because the ball
explanation_steps: Heating made the ball expand (get bigger).

questions.stem: The step of a scientific method used to prove a hypothesis is:
explanation_steps: Steps of the scientific method: identify the problem → observe → make a hypothesis → do an experiment → make a conclusion.
The textbook says: 'In order to prove the hypothesis, scientists do experiments.' Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Scientists do an experiment to test (prove) their hypothesis.
tips: Hypothesis = a scientific guess. Experiment = the test of the guess.

similar_questions.stem: A scientific guess that must be tested is called
explanation_steps: A hypothesis is a scientific guess based on observations.

questions.stem: If a machine does a work of 100 J in 5 seconds. How much power will the machine use?
explanation_steps: Power = work ÷ time (P = W ÷ t).
Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 72)
questions.explain_simple: Power = work ÷ time = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 watts.
tips: P = W ÷ t. Unit: joule per second = watt (W).

similar_questions.stem: A boy does 600 J of work in 20 s. What is his power?

questions.stem: Which of the following farm tools is used for digging hard soil?
explanation_steps: Table 5.1 of the Grade 7 textbook: Hoe – digging hard soil.
Axe – cutting and splitting wood. Rake – preparing seed-beds and collecting weeds. Fork – collecting and spreading crops, grass or manure.
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A hoe is used to dig hard soil.
tips: Learn each farm tool with its use (textbook Table 5.1).

similar_questions.stem: Which farm tool is used for harvesting crops and cutting grass?
explanation_steps: A sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops and grass.

questions.stem: Plants that can produce their own food by photosynthesis are called:
explanation_steps: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, using sunlight.
Because they make (produce) food, they are called producers.
Consumers eat other living things, carnivores eat meat, decomposers break down dead things. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 126)
questions.explain_simple: Green plants make their own food, so they are producers.
tips: Producer = makes food. Consumer = eats food.

similar_questions.stem: In a food chain, a grasshopper that eats grass is a
explanation_steps: The grasshopper eats a producer (grass), so it is a primary consumer (herbivore).

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a unisexual plant?
explanation_steps: A unisexual organism has only a male or only a female sex.
The textbook gives papaya as a unisexual plant: one papaya plant has male flowers and another plant has female flowers.
Beans and peas have both sexes in one flower (bisexual). Maize has separate male and female flowers but on the SAME plant, so the plant has both sexes. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: A papaya tree is only male or only female. So papaya is a unisexual plant.
tips: Beans/peas: both parts in one flower. Maize: two kinds of flowers on one plant. Papaya: male and female plants.

similar_questions.stem: Which plant has both male and female parts in one flower?
explanation_steps: Beans have male and female parts in a single flower (bisexual flower).

questions.stem: One of the following shows a balanced force. Identify it: (four force diagrams A–D)
questions.image_alt: Four diagrams of a box with two 10 N forces. A: both arrows point up (one below, one on top). B: both arrows point down. C: one arrow pushes right on the left side and one pushes left on the right side. D: one arrow points left away from the left side and one pushes left on the right side.

options.A: Diagram A: F1 = 10 N up from below and F2 = 10 N up on top
options.B: Diagram B: F2 = 10 N down on top and F1 = 10 N down below
options.C: Diagram C: F1 = 10 N pushing right on the left side and F2 = 10 N pushing left on the right side
options.D: Diagram D: F1 = 10 N pulling left on the left side and F2 = 10 N pushing left on the right side

explanation_steps: Forces are balanced when they are equal in size and act in opposite directions. Then the net force is zero.
In A both forces point up (net 20 N up). In B both point down (net 20 N down). In D both point left (net 20 N left).
In C, 10 N pushes to the right and 10 N pushes to the left: 10 − 10 = 0. This is balanced. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 49)
questions.explain_simple: In C the two 10 N forces push in opposite directions. They cancel, so they are balanced.
tips: Balanced = same size + opposite directions → net force 0.

similar_questions.stem: A 30 N force pulls a box to the left and a 30 N force pulls it to the right. The box
explanation_steps: Equal and opposite forces are balanced, so the net force is zero and the box does not start to move.

questions.stem: All of the following are correct about the nucleus of an atom, except:

options.D: made up of protons and neutrons

explanation_steps: The nucleus is the small, heavy centre of the atom. It has protons (+) and neutrons (no charge), so it is positively charged.
The energy levels (electron shells) are OUTSIDE the nucleus, in the atomic shell, where the electrons move.
So the wrong statement is B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 75)
questions.explain_simple: Energy levels are outside the nucleus. The nucleus has only protons and neutrons.
tips: Nucleus: protons + neutrons. Shells (energy levels): electrons.

similar_questions.stem: Which particles move in the energy levels around the nucleus?
explanation_steps: Electrons move in the shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.

questions.stem:
In the following word equation identify the product(s):
Magnesium + Oxygen → Magnesium Oxide
explanation_steps: Reactants are on the left of the arrow; products are on the right.
The right side has only magnesium oxide. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 90)
questions.explain_simple: The product is after the arrow: magnesium oxide.
tips: Before the arrow = reactants. After the arrow = products.

similar_questions.stem: Iron + Sulphur → Iron sulphide. The reactants are
explanation_steps: The reactants are on the left: iron and sulphur.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in one molecule of Calcium Carbonate (CaCO₃)?
explanation_steps: CaCO₃ has 1 calcium atom (Ca), 1 carbon atom (C) and 3 oxygen atoms (O₃).
Total = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 atoms. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 86)
tips: The small number after a symbol tells how many atoms of that element.

similar_questions.stem: How many atoms are in one molecule of water (H₂O)?
explanation_steps: 2 hydrogen atoms + 1 oxygen atom = 3 atoms.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of elements represents metals?
explanation_steps: Metals are shiny and conduct heat and electricity well: iron, silver, copper, aluminium, sodium, calcium.
Chlorine, carbon and nitrogen are non-metals.
Only A has two metals. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 106; Science Grade 8, p. 93)
questions.explain_simple: Iron and silver are both metals.
tips: Check both elements in the pair. One non-metal makes the pair wrong.

similar_questions.stem: Which pair are both non-metals?
explanation_steps: Oxygen and sulphur are both non-metals.

questions.stem: Objects that can be good radiators and absorbers of heat are:
explanation_steps: Black, dull (rough) surfaces are good absorbers and good radiators of heat.
White, shiny and smooth surfaces reflect heat, so they are poor absorbers and poor radiators.
Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 114)
questions.explain_simple: Black and rough surfaces take in and give out heat well.
tips: Dark and dull = good absorber and radiator. White and shiny = good reflector.

similar_questions.stem: Why do people in hot places often wear white clothes?
explanation_steps: White surfaces reflect heat, so the body stays cooler.

questions.stem: A thermometer reading shows 86°F (degree Fahrenheit). What is this temperature in °C (degree Centigrade)?
explanation_steps: Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 122)
tips: °C = 5/9 × (°F − 32). Subtract 32 first!

similar_questions.stem: Change 212 °F to °C.

questions.stem: Each pair of chromosomes is attached to one another by a:
explanation_steps: In a body cell chromosomes are in pairs.
The textbook says: 'Each pair of chromosomes is attached to one another by a centromere.'
Genes are parts of chromosomes; meiosis and mitosis are kinds of cell division. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A centromere holds the two chromosomes of a pair together.
tips: Centromere = the 'button' that joins a pair of chromosomes.

similar_questions.stem: The units of heredity that are found on chromosomes are called
explanation_steps: Genes are found on chromosomes and carry traits from parents to offspring.

questions.stem: A type of satellite that helps ships to know their exact location or position is
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Navigation satellites help ships and airplanes to know their exact location.'
Weather satellites watch the weather; communication satellites carry TV, radio and phone signals. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Navigation satellites tell ships and planes where they are.
tips: Navigation = finding your way.

similar_questions.stem: Which satellite sends TV and telephone signals around the world?
explanation_steps: Communication satellites carry TV, radio and phone signals.

questions.stem: The process of changing matter from a solid state to a liquid state is called:
explanation_steps: Changes of state: solid → liquid = melting; liquid → solid = freezing; liquid → gas = boiling/evaporation; gas → liquid = condensation.
Solid to liquid is melting, for example ice becoming water. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 49)
questions.explain_simple: When a solid becomes a liquid, it melts. Ice melts into water.
tips: Melting is the opposite of freezing.

similar_questions.stem: Water vapour on a cold window becomes water drops. This is
explanation_steps: Gas → liquid is condensation.

questions.stem: An example of renewable natural resource is:
explanation_steps: Renewable resources are replaced by nature: air, water, soil, sunlight.
Fuel (oil), iron and coal cannot be replaced once they are used: they are non-renewable. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 187)
questions.explain_simple: Air is always renewed by nature. It is a renewable resource.
tips: Renewable: air, water, soil, sunlight, plants.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Oil cannot be made again quickly, so it is non-renewable.

questions.stem: Identify the chemical symbol of mercury:
explanation_steps: Mercury's symbol is Hg, from its Latin name Hydrargyrum.
Fe = iron, Al = aluminium, Au = gold. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 85)
questions.explain_simple: The symbol of mercury is Hg.
tips: Some symbols come from Latin names: Fe (iron), Na (sodium), Ag (silver), Hg (mercury).

similar_questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol of silver?
explanation_steps: Silver is Ag, from its Latin name Argentum.

questions.stem: A sex characteristic seen only in male is:

options.A: menstruation starts at about every 28 days
options.C: growth of hairs on the armpits

explanation_steps: At puberty, the voice of boys becomes deeper.
Hair grows in the armpits of BOTH boys and girls, so C is not only male and D is wrong.
Menstruation happens only in girls. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 189)
questions.explain_simple: Only boys get a deeper voice at puberty. Armpit hair grows in boys and girls.
tips: Watch for 'only': check if the change happens in both sexes.

similar_questions.stem: A body change seen only in girls at puberty is
explanation_steps: Breasts enlarge only in girls. The other changes happen in both sexes.

questions.stem: A car traveling at 4m/s increases its speed uniformly to 12m/s in 2 seconds. What is its acceleration?
explanation_steps: a = (final velocity − initial velocity) ÷ time.
Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 58)
questions.explain_simple: The speed grows by 8 m/s in 2 s. 8 ÷ 2 = 4 m/s².
tips: Subtract first, then divide by time.

similar_questions.stem: A runner goes from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. Her acceleration is

questions.stem: Identify the three basic organelles of a cell.

options.A: cell membrane, cytoplasm, and cell wall

explanation_steps: Every living cell (plant or animal) has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus. These are the basic contents of a cell.
The cell wall and chloroplasts are found only in plant cells. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 102)
questions.explain_simple: All cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus.
tips: Basic parts of every cell: membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus.

similar_questions.stem: Which part controls all the activities of the cell?
explanation_steps: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell.

questions.stem: Transfer of heat through a vacuum is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'The transfer of heat through a vacuum or empty space is called radiation.'
Conduction and convection need matter. Reflection is heat bouncing off a surface. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Heat moves through empty space by radiation, like heat from the Sun.
tips: Vacuum → radiation only.

similar_questions.stem: You feel warm when you sit near a fire. The heat reaches you mainly by
explanation_steps: Heat from a fire travels to you as radiation.

questions.stem: The earth's atmosphere has 4 layers. The uppermost layer is known as:
explanation_steps: From the ground up the layers are: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.
The thermosphere is above the mesosphere; it is the top (uppermost) layer. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 148-149)
questions.explain_simple: The top layer of the atmosphere is the thermosphere.
tips: T-S-M-T: Troposphere (bottom) … Thermosphere (top).

similar_questions.stem: Which layer of the atmosphere is between the stratosphere and the thermosphere?
explanation_steps: The order is troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.

questions.stem: Over 97% of the earth's water is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says over 97% of the earth's water is salty (in the seas and oceans); the rest is fresh water.
Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Almost all water on Earth is sea water, which is salty.
tips: 97% salty, less than 3% fresh.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the fresh water on Earth is found as
explanation_steps: Most fresh water is frozen as ice at the poles and on high mountains.

questions.stem: The number of complete vibrations of an object in one second is called:
explanation_steps: The number of vibrations of a vibrating body in one second is called frequency.
Hertz (Hz) is the UNIT of frequency, not its name. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 204)
questions.explain_simple: Vibrations in one second = frequency. We measure it in hertz.
tips: Frequency is the quantity; hertz is the unit.

similar_questions.stem: A string vibrates 50 times in one second. Its frequency is
explanation_steps: 50 vibrations per second = 50 hertz.

questions.stem: A shadow of an object is formed, because:
explanation_steps: Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot bend around an opaque object.
The dark area behind the object, where light cannot reach, is the shadow. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 63; Science Grade 6, p. 65)
questions.explain_simple: Light goes in straight lines. It cannot go around an object, so a shadow forms.
tips: Shadows and eclipses happen because light travels in straight lines.

similar_questions.stem: A shadow is formed when light falls on
explanation_steps: An opaque object blocks the light, so a shadow forms behind it.

questions.stem: Nitrogen and Oxygen gases in the air are respectively represented as:
explanation_steps: 'Respectively' means in the same order: first nitrogen, then oxygen.
Air is 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 86)
questions.explain_simple: Nitrogen is 78% and oxygen is 21% of air.
tips: 'Respectively' = in the same order as the names.

similar_questions.stem: About what percentage of the air is oxygen?
explanation_steps: Oxygen is about 21% of the air.

questions.stem: Numbers 2 and 3 of the flower in this figure are:
questions.image_alt: A hand-drawn flower. Label 1 points to a green sepal below the flower, 2 to the big outer petal, 3 to an oval anther on a stalk, and 4 to the top of the middle stalk (stigma).
explanation_steps: In the drawing, 1 points to the green leaf-like parts under the flower (sepals).
2 points to the large coloured outer part (petal). 3 points to the small oval head on a stalk (anther, part of the stamen). 4 points to the top of the middle part (stigma of the pistil).
So 2 = petal and 3 = anther. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 121-122)
questions.explain_simple: Number 2 is a petal and number 3 is an anther.
tips: Outside to inside: sepals → petals → stamens (anther) → pistil (stigma).

similar_questions.stem: Which part of a flower makes pollen grains?
explanation_steps: The anther (top of the stamen) makes pollen grains.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Structure and Function in Living Things

questions.stem: In the human body, the brain and spinal cord are:
explanation_steps: Stimulus → receptor → coordinator → effector → response.
The coordinator is the brain or spinal cord. It organises the right response.
Receptors (like the eye) detect the stimulus; effectors (muscles, glands) produce the response. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 84)
questions.explain_simple: The brain and spinal cord decide what to do. They are coordinators.
tips: Receptor detects, coordinator decides, effector acts.

similar_questions.stem: In the body, muscles and glands that produce a response are called
explanation_steps: Effectors (muscles or glands) carry out the response.

questions.stem: Find the work done, if a force of 12N is used to move a box to a distance of 4m.
explanation_steps: Work = force × distance.
W = 12 N × 4 m = 48 J. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 59)
questions.explain_simple: Work = 12 × 4 = 48 joules.
tips: Work (J) = force (N) × distance (m).

similar_questions.stem: How much work is done when a 25 N force moves a cart 2 m?

questions.stem: Animals that feed both on plants and other animals are:
explanation_steps: Herbivores eat only plants; carnivores eat only animals.
Omnivores are consumers that eat both plants and animals (for example people).
'Consumers' includes all three groups, so it is not the best answer. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 126)
questions.explain_simple: Animals that eat plants and meat are omnivores.
tips: herbi = plants, carni = meat, omni = all.

similar_questions.stem: A lion eats only other animals. It is a
explanation_steps: Animals that eat only meat are carnivores.

questions.stem: The type of joint represented by letter "A" in the table below is:
explanation_steps: The table says: joint 'A' is found in the elbow and allows movement in one direction only.
The hinge joint is found in the elbow, knee and fingers and allows movement in one plane only, like a door hinge. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 31)
questions.explain_simple: The elbow moves in one direction. It is a hinge joint.
tips: Elbow and knee = hinge. Shoulder and hip = ball and socket.

similar_questions.stem: Which joint is found in the skull and does not move?
explanation_steps: The bones of the skull are joined by fixed joints that do not move.

questions.stem: The combination of all the forces acting on an object is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A net force is the combination of all the forces acting on an object.'
Velocity and speed describe motion, not forces. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: All forces together make the net force.
tips: Net force = total force after adding/subtracting.

similar_questions.stem: Two forces of 8 N and 5 N push a box in the same direction. The net force is
explanation_steps: Same direction: 8 + 5 = 13 N.

questions.stem: Traits passed on from parents to offspring are called:
explanation_steps: Inherited traits are passed from parents to their children through genes (eye colour, blood group).
Acquired traits come from the environment or learning (a scar, riding a bicycle). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 141)
questions.explain_simple: Traits from parents are inherited traits.
tips: Inherited = from parents. Acquired = during your life.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is an acquired trait?
explanation_steps: A scar is caused by an injury during life, so it is acquired.

questions.stem: In order to escape from earth's gravitational attraction, rockets are launched at a speed of:
explanation_steps: The textbook says a rocket must be launched at a very high speed, about 11 km/s, to escape the earth's gravity.
11 km/s is 11 000 metres every second. 11 km/h or 11 m/s is only as fast as a bicycle or a car. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A rocket needs about 11 km every second to escape the Earth's gravity.
tips: Escape speed from Earth ≈ 11 km/s.

similar_questions.stem: Rockets must go very fast to leave the Earth because of
explanation_steps: The Earth's gravity pulls the rocket back, so it needs a very high speed.

questions.stem: What is the time needed to travel 4,500m for a sound travelling at the speed of 1,500m/s?
explanation_steps: time = distance ÷ speed.
Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208-209)
questions.explain_simple: Time = distance ÷ speed = 4500 ÷ 1500 = 3 seconds.
tips: t = s ÷ v. The units m ÷ (m/s) give seconds.

similar_questions.stem: Sound travels 1 700 m in air at 340 m/s. How long does it take?

questions.stem: Which cell organelle controls things that pass into or out of a cell?
explanation_steps: The cell membrane surrounds the cytoplasm. It controls what goes into and out of the cell.
The nucleus controls the cell's activities; mitochondria release energy. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 104)
questions.explain_simple: The cell membrane is like a gate. It controls what enters and leaves the cell.
tips: Membrane = gate; nucleus = control centre; mitochondria = power house.

similar_questions.stem: Which part of the cell releases energy from food?
explanation_steps: Mitochondria release energy for the cell.

questions.stem: One of the following statements is correct. Identify it.

options.A: an element can be divided into simpler substances by chemical means
options.B: a compound can be separated into its elements by physical means
options.C: sugar dissolved in water forms a heterogeneous mixture
options.D: a mixture can be separated into its constituents by physical means

explanation_steps: A: wrong – an element is the simplest substance; it cannot be broken down.
B: wrong – a compound needs chemical means to separate its elements.
C: wrong – sugar in water looks the same everywhere, so it is a homogeneous mixture (a solution).
D: correct – a mixture can be separated by physical means (filtering, evaporation, using a magnet). Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 44)
questions.explain_simple: Mixtures can be separated by physical ways, like filtering or using a magnet.
tips: Mixture → physical separation. Compound → chemical separation. Element → cannot be broken down.

similar_questions.stem: Iron filings mixed with sand can be separated by
explanation_steps: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet pulls the iron out of the sand (a physical method).

questions.stem: Glands in the wall of the stomach secrete:
explanation_steps: Glands in the stomach wall secrete gastric juice, which helps digest proteins.
Bile comes from the liver; pancreatic juice from the pancreas; intestinal juice from the small intestine. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 7)
questions.explain_simple: The stomach makes gastric juice.
tips: Mouth – saliva; stomach – gastric juice; liver – bile; pancreas – pancreatic juice.

similar_questions.stem: Which digestive juice is made by the liver?
explanation_steps: The liver makes bile, which helps digest fats.

questions.stem: Heat moves by convectional current in:
explanation_steps: Convection happens in fluids (liquids and gases), because their particles can move.
Air is a gas, so heat moves in air by convection currents.
Glass, wood and paper are solids: heat moves in them by conduction. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 108)
questions.explain_simple: Convection happens in liquids and gases, like air.
tips: Solids → conduction; liquids and gases → convection.

similar_questions.stem: Water in a pot gets hot everywhere because of
explanation_steps: Hot water rises and cold water sinks. This makes convection currents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of global warming?

options.C: melting of ice in the poles

explanation_steps: Global warming is the rise in the average temperature of the earth.
The textbook says: 'Ice at the poles will melt; the sea level will rise and floods…'
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: When the Earth gets warmer, ice at the poles melts.
tips: Global warming → ice melts → sea level rises.

similar_questions.stem: Global warming is mainly caused by too much of which gas in the air?
explanation_steps: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, so the Earth gets warmer.
